craft_notes: Sthāyin: ānanda as rejoicing consciousness (hṛṣṭi); vyabhicāri wonder at rarity fenced. Sanskrit-first: nṛtyati/gāyati (DANCES/SINGS — kept tripled with rejoices: joy in three verbs); samaya-vid (COVENANT-KNOWERS — fenced term kept fenced AND translated: fence is doctrine); durlabha (HARD-to-obtain — kept). Rows: 9 (dances/sings/rejoices triple — tripled joy), 7 (‘O Bhairava, Lord’ mid-verse — address INSIDE the dance, joy first), 1 (‘covenant’ closes — rarity fenced last). Close: ‘kept for knowers of the covenant’. Rupture: colon after ‘Lord’ (dancing turns to defining — joy, then what joy means: obtaining = vision per C1). Rejected: ‘my beloved’ — killed: priya kept plain; explaining samaya — killed: un-fencing would un-fence the doctrine; ‘rare’ alone — killed: ‘hard for others to obtain’ keeps the exclusivity structure. Read aloud: THIS-con-SCIOUS-ness OF-mine DAN-ces, SINGS, re-JOI-ces DEEP-ly — o-BHAI-ra-va, LORD: HAV-ing-WON-you, my-DEAR — a-SING-le BEAU-ti-ful VI-sion … KEPT for KNOW-ers OF the COV-e-nant.

lines: This consciousness of mine dances, sings, rejoices deeply — O Bhairava, Lord:
having won You, my dear — a single beautiful vision, hard for others to obtain, kept for knowers of the covenant.
l4.sanskrit_cite: nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍham saṃvit iyam mama bhairavanātha tvāṃ priyam āpya sudarśanamekam durlabhamanyajanaiḥ samayajñam
notes: sudarśanam ekam as ‘a single beautiful vision’ (boundary open); samayajñam as qualifier (fence), with C1

reads_against.argmap: What is obtaining, and who obtains? → Joy, then its cause: obtaining is vision, rare by structure and fenced to the initiated.
c1_essence: Consciousness dances and sings; obtaining the Lord is defined as rare vision — fenced to the initiated.
Joy first, then its cause named: obtaining = vision, rare by structure.
It moves from rejoicing to the definition of obtaining as vision, fenced to the knower of the samaya.
